differences.what: No pergola roof or timber frame. The reference is a covered corridor with a clear glass/polycarbonate roof on dark-wood beams and cross-joists, and thick dark posts every ~2m on both sides. The capture is open to the sky.
differences.where: Whole upper half of frame; posts along the left and right railings
differences.fix: Build a pergola over the full terrace length: dark-stained wood posts (~15cm square) along both rails, longitudinal beams at ~2.6m, cross-joists every ~0.6m, and a transparent roof panel with wet streaks, droplets and water sheeting off the edges as thin falling curtains. Rain should fall outside this roof and not through it onto the tables.

differences.what: Overall lighting is cold blue moonlight with no warm sources. The reference is dominated by warm amber/orange light from the heaters, lanterns, string bulbs, candles and under-planter LED strips, with only small teal/cyan accents.
differences.where: Entire frame, especially the deck, the railings and the right side
differences.fix: Make the key light warm (about 2200-2700K). Add point lights at each heater element, lantern and bulb, plus warm LED strip lights under the planter lips and at the deck edge. Drop the blue fill to a low ambient and use bloom so the light sources glow.

differences.what: The railings are flat, untextured gray-lavender panels. The reference has vertical dark-wood slat fences topped by long wooden planter boxes overflowing with ivy, hanging purple wisteria, white/pink flowers and lush foliage, plus tall bamboo on the right.
differences.where: Left and right railings, running the full depth
differences.fix: Replace the panels with vertical wood-slat fencing (warm brown, visible gaps) and put a planter trough on top. Fill the left planters with trailing ivy and wisteria racemes hanging 0.5-1m down the fence face, and the right ones with dense shrubs, pink blossoms and a 3m bamboo cluster at the far right, all lit from below.

differences.what: The floor is a flat matte dark-blue plane with no reflections. The reference deck is glossy wet wood planks that mirror every warm light as long streaky reflections.
differences.where: Deck floor, center foreground to the vanishing point
differences.fix: Use plank-patterned dark-wood decking with very low roughness (about 0.05-0.15), puddle masks and screen-space/planar reflections so the heaters, candles and string lights reflect as elongated amber streaks. Add rain ripples and splashes on the deck.

differences.what: The patio heaters are wrong and badly placed. They are flat orange/beige untextured cylinders with a lampshade cap, and one fills the right foreground. The reference heaters are polished copper/brass poles with a glowing orange wire-mesh heating tube and a wide reflective dish cap, set back mid-right.
differences.where: Right side; the foreground heater at the far right edge and the second at center-right
differences.fix: Model a metallic copper heater: a base cylinder, a slim pole, a ~1m glowing mesh cage with an emissive orange element and a 1m reflector dish. Place two along the right rail at about 3m and 6m depth. Remove the giant foreground column so the frame's right side shows planters and the sign instead.

differences.what: The paper lanterns are missing. The reference has three round white paper chochin lanterns with a water-drop logo, glowing warm, hanging from the left posts, plus a small one further back on the right.
differences.where: Upper left, hanging from the posts at about 1/4, 1/3 and 2/5 of frame width
differences.fix: Add emissive white paper lanterns with the 雫 water-drop-and-waves emblem printed on them, hanging from the left posts at about head height and decreasing in size with depth, plus one small lantern on the far right post.

differences.what: The string lights are off and the wrong scale. The capture shows huge flat-colored unlit discs looped across open sky. The reference has small glowing warm-white bulbs with occasional red/teal/pink ones, zig-zagging under the roof beams along the whole corridor.
differences.where: Top center to the vanishing point
differences.fix: Shrink the bulbs to about 6cm and make them emissive with bloom, mostly warm white with a few colored. Hang them in a zigzag between the beams under the roof all the way to the back, and add their reflections on the deck.

differences.what: The tables and stools are low-poly, flat-shaded orange decagons. The reference has round, glossy marble/brass-rimmed tables on black pedestal bases and plump red leather stool cushions with chrome legs and footrings. The reference also shows 4 tables receding, where the capture has 2.
differences.where: Center: the table group and the four visible stools; also the far end of the corridor
differences.fix: Use smooth round tops (24+ segments) in a light glossy material with a metal edge, and black cast bases. Make the stools tufted red leather with specular highlights and rain beads on chrome frames. Line 4 tables down the corridor with stools on both sides.

differences.what: The tabletop props and signage are missing. The reference has a menu card stand, a glowing candle in glass, a small vase with pink flowers and a steaming teacup on each table, plus a dark plaque reading 関係者以外立入禁止 on the right fence, a stone lantern floor light at the bottom right, a pink neon 雫テラス sign at the top right and a red やきとり sign at the left.
differences.where: Tabletops (center); the right fence at mid-height; the bottom-right corner; the top-right corner; the far left mid-height
differences.fix: Add a candle (emissive plus point light), a white menu stand, a bud vase and a teacup with a steam particle to each table. Mount the 関係者以外立入禁止 plaque on the right fence, place a glowing stone/wood lantern at the bottom right, and add the pink neon 雫テラス sign with a drop icon and a red-lit やきとり shop sign visible over the left rail.

differences.what: The rain treatment is wrong and the background is too dark and flat. Dense white rain streaks cover the whole frame, including the covered area. The background buildings are dark navy boxes with few lit windows. In the reference, rain shows mainly as dripping curtains off the roof edges and fine streaks against the buildings, and the buildings have many warm lit windows, balconies, AC units and cyan neon edge strips.
differences.where: Entire frame (rain); background buildings left, center and right
differences.fix: Cull rain particles under the roof, add drip lines falling from the roof edges, and keep thin, lower-opacity streaks only outside. Light about 50% of the background windows in warm interior colors, add balcony railings and a cyan neon strip along the building ledges at about the roof height, and add slight depth fog for atmospheric falloff.
